scenes.visual: Title card 'Holding a Boulder Still' over a cartoon intertidal boulder field. COLOUR MAP, same in both films: species 1 TEAL, species 2 GOLD, species 3 VIOLET, species 4 CORAL dots; the effective number is always a row of identical NAVY 'equal species' columns; the order dial is a semicircle labelled q = 0, 1, 2; on the shore, Ulva GREEN, barnacles GREY, Gigartina RED. Cream background, 16:9. Every number appears only as on-screen text. Effective numbers are computed (label 'computed'); anything not computed is labelled 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: Succession needs time, but on a rocky shore, winter waves keep turning boulders over. Middle-sized boulders hold the most diverse communities. Is that because of their size, or because of how often waves turn them?
scenes.visual: A shore of boulders of three sizes fades in; the intermediate boulder carries a label 'most diverse'. A question mark sits between a ruler icon labelled 'size' and a curling wave labelled 'overturning'.
scenes.narration: Succession needs time, but on a rocky shore, winter waves keep turning boulders over. Middle-sized boulders hold the most diverse communities. Is that because of their size, or because of how often waves turn them?

scenes.tts: Wayne Sousa studied a boulder field on the southern California coast. There, winter storm waves overturn the boulders.
scenes.visual: Name card 'Wayne Sousa, Ecology, 1979'. A map pin on the southern California coast. A winter storm wave rolls in and tips one boulder over, showing its upper face going under.
scenes.narration: Wayne Sousa studied a boulder field on the southern California coast. There, winter storm waves overturn the boulders.

scenes.tts: Overturning a boulder kills some or all of the algae on its upper face, and opens space. So each turn sets succession on that surface back.
scenes.visual: Close-up of one boulder's upper face covered in green and red algae. The boulder flips; when it rights itself, most of the cover is gone, a few red tufts survive (label 'survivors can regrow'), and bare rock is exposed. Schematic.
scenes.narration: Overturning a boulder kills some or all of the algae on its upper face, and opens space. So each turn sets succession on that surface back.

scenes.tts: Picture a clock on each upper face, counting time since it was last cleared. On a fully cleared face, Ulva and barnacles usually settled first. Red algae followed. Without another overturning, Gigartina often came to dominate. Survivors can change that order.
scenes.visual: A ring-shaped clock drawn on a boulder top, labelled 'time since last cleared', with four sectors in the usual order on a fully cleared face: 'bare rock' (beige), 'Ulva + barnacles' (GREEN and GREY), 'mixed' (green, grey and red patches), 'Gigartina' (RED). A hand sweeps slowly around. A small caption: 'usual order on a cleared face; survivors can change it'. Schematic.
scenes.narration: Picture a clock on each upper face, counting time since it was last cleared. On a fully cleared face, Ulva and barnacles usually settled first. Red algae followed. Without another overturning, Gigartina often came to dominate. Survivors can change that order.

scenes.tts: Small boulders are overturned often, so their clocks keep snapping back. They carry sparse early communities of Ulva and barnacles. Large boulders rarely turn, and Gigartina takes them over.
scenes.visual: Three boulders side by side: small, intermediate, large, each with its clock. Waves sweep through repeatedly. The small boulder flips again and again and its hand keeps jumping back to the green-grey sector. The large boulder never moves; its hand reaches the red sector and its top fills with red.
scenes.narration: Small boulders are overturned often, so their clocks keep snapping back. They carry sparse early communities of Ulva and barnacles. Large boulders rarely turn, and Gigartina takes them over.

scenes.tts: Boulders of intermediate size turn now and then. They are caught partway along, and they carry the most diverse communities.
scenes.visual: The intermediate boulder flips occasionally; its hand stops in the 'mixed' sector, its top shows green, grey and several red shades. Above each boulder a small navy 'equal species' row appears, tallest over the intermediate boulder. Label 'schematic: not Sousa's values'.
scenes.narration: Boulders of intermediate size turn now and then. They are caught partway along, and they carry the most diverse communities.

scenes.tts: But size and overturning travel together. The small rocks are the ones that flip. A bigger surface might simply hold more species, so the pattern alone cannot say which matters.
scenes.visual: Two arrows, 'size' and 'how often overturned', glide side by side from small to large boulders, locked together by a chain labelled 'confounded'. A small inset shows surface area growing with boulder size.
scenes.narration: But size and overturning travel together. The small rocks are the ones that flip. A bigger surface might simply hold more species, so the pattern alone cannot say which matters.

scenes.tts: So Sousa held some small boulders still, fixed in place so waves could not turn them. Similar small boulders were left loose nearby, free to roll. Both sets sat at the same height on the shore.
scenes.visual: Two groups of small boulders at the same tidal height. One group is fixed to a frame anchored in the rock, with a padlock icon labelled 'fixed: cannot overturn'. The other group sits loose beside it, labelled 'loose: free to roll'. The chain between 'size' and 'overturning' snaps.
scenes.narration: So Sousa held some small boulders still, fixed in place so waves could not turn them. Similar small boulders were left loose nearby, free to roll. Both sets sat at the same height on the shore.

scenes.tts: If size is what matters, the fixed small boulders should stay sparse. If overturning is what matters, what should they become?
scenes.visual: Both groups shown with their clocks paused at the green-grey sector. A time bar labelled '1975 to early 1977' sits above them, unfilled. Two option tags: 'stay sparse' and '?'.
scenes.narration: If size is what matters, the fixed small boulders should stay sparse. If overturning is what matters, what should they become?

scenes.visual: Hold the frame; a 5-second countdown; caption 'Predict: what do the fixed small boulders become?'.

scenes.tts: They moved on. Ulva gave way, and red algae, Gigartina among them, came to cover most of the fixed rocks. The loose rocks kept their early communities.
scenes.visual: The time bar fills. On the fixed rocks the clock hand advances into the late 'mixed' sector, edging toward 'Gigartina'; GREEN Ulva fades and several RED algae spread over most of each top. The loose rocks keep flipping in storms and stay green and grey. Schematic.
scenes.narration: They moved on. Ulva gave way, and red algae, Gigartina among them, came to cover most of the fixed rocks. The loose rocks kept their early communities.

scenes.tts: The fixed small boulders became as species-rich and diverse as larger, intermediate-sized boulders. Their smaller surface did not stop them. On that shore, how often rocks overturned, not surface area alone, accounted for the pattern.
scenes.visual: The navy 'equal species' row over a fixed small boulder grows to match the row over an intermediate boulder; a label 'as species-rich and diverse as larger, intermediate-sized boulders'. Banner: 'on this shore: overturning frequency, not surface area alone'.
scenes.narration: The fixed small boulders became as species-rich and diverse as larger, intermediate-sized boulders. Their smaller surface did not stop them. On that shore, how often rocks overturned, not surface area alone, accounted for the pattern.

scenes.tts: This test varied one thing, how often a patch is reset. It did not vary how hard each event hits, and it holds for one shore. Even there, the season of a census mattered. In spring, large boulders were no longer poorer in species.
scenes.visual: A control panel with two sliders: 'how often' (moved during the film, highlighted) and 'how hard' (greyed out, untouched). A small map pin labelled 'one shore'.
scenes.narration: This test varied one thing, how often a patch is reset. It did not vary how hard each event hits, and it holds for one shore. Even there, the season of a census mattered. In spring, large boulders were no longer poorer in species.

scenes.tts: So disturbance sets succession back, and how often it strikes helps decide how far a patch gets.
scenes.visual: The three original boulders return with their clocks; a dial labelled 'how often disturbed' turns from frequent to rare, and the clock hand on a single boulder travels further around as the dial moves toward rare.
scenes.narration: So disturbance sets succession back, and how often it strikes helps decide how far a patch gets.

scenes.visual: Hex end card. Take-home line: 'How often disturbance strikes helps set how far succession gets.'
